forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Lambeth's £116m exceptional financial support approved in principle, with asset sales planned
news_drafts.lead:
Lambeth Council's application for £116m of exceptional financial support, which is government permission to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending, has been approved in principle by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. The council's quarter 2 financial performance report for 2026/27 says so in the papers for Cabinet's meeting on 25 November. The support covers 2024/25 to 2026/27 in declining amounts, and the quarter 2 budget table shows £20m of it.

The paper says the support was used to increase reserves and provisions, meet the 2025/26 overspend and balance the 2026/27 budget. It says "the Council expects to fund EFS by a planned programme of asset disposals". Any disposal decisions will follow the council's Strategic Asset Management Framework and formal approval. A separate quarter 2 budget monitor gives an update on the disposals programme, which it describes as "aimed at repaying" the support, alongside the forecast capital spend for the year. The list of assets in the disposal pipeline is in a Part II appendix that is exempt from disclosure, and the extract gives no total.

Because Lambeth is an exceptional financial support council, the paper says "an independent third-party review is currently being undertaken by" the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy. The Ministry will scrutinise progress on asset sales and savings delivery, and the council expects regular meetings with it.

news_drafts.headline: Lambeth's £40m exceptional support loan from 2025/26 is to be repaid from housing asset disposals
news_drafts.lead:
Lambeth received £40m of exceptional financial support in 2025/26 and must repay it, according to the Asset Management Strategy put to its Overview and Scrutiny Committee on 24 November 2026. Exceptional financial support is government permission to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending. The report names the sale of housing revenue account assets as the route to repayment. The housing revenue account is the ring-fenced account for the council's own housing stock, paid for by rents. The assets in question are those that are non-operational or beyond economic repair.

The report says the council "received £40m of Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) to address its disrepair backlog. This funding is a loan and therefore repayable." It also says no further request for exceptional financial support is currently anticipated for 2026/27.

The strategy sets out the sales so far and those planned. Residential disposals achieved £3.318m in 2025/26. Garages, land, residential properties and hostels valued at more than £13m have been identified and recommended for disposal this financial year. The report says they would come to market around the fourth quarter of 2026/27. Income from disposals is to be applied to repaying the loan.

news_drafts.headline: Lambeth plans asset disposals to repay £116m of government-approved exceptional financial support
news_drafts.lead:
Lambeth Council expects to repay £116m of exceptional financial support through a planned programme of asset disposals, its second-quarter papers for 2026/27 say. Exceptional financial support is government permission to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending. The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government approved the council's application in principle in February 2026, for amounts declining across 2024/25 to 2026/27.

The quarter 2 financial performance report says the support allowed the council to increase reserves and provisions at the end of 2024/25, meet the 2025/26 overspend and balance the 2026/27 budget. It says the ministry will increase its scrutiny of progress. The quarter 2 budget monitor gives an update on the disposals programme. It asks members to note an indicative disposal pipeline for the general fund and for the housing revenue account, the ring-fenced account for council housing. A second pipeline, in a confidential Part II appendix, is to go through formal decision reports.

The Finance and Budget Scrutiny Committee has asked officers for a report on the council's stance on asset disposals to repay the support. It is to cover asset categories, progress to date and a timeline by financial year, for both accounts, and the committee wants it before any Cabinet decision. Officers have said disposal information will be included in the quarter 2 report.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - September 26 (Q2) Financial Performance Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: SME invoices paid within 10 days reached 71% in Quarter 2, against an 80% target and up from 64% in Quarter 1.
findings.detail: The paper reports that overall invoices paid within 30 days met the 96% target. The SME measure remains below target.
findings.matters: Payment performance to SMEs is a supplier-market indicator that finance officers and lenders monitor alongside the council's cash management.
findings.figures: 71% SME invoices paid within 10 days; 80% target; 64% in Quarter 1; 96% of all invoices paid within 30 days
findings.quote: SME performance for Q2 stands at 71%, an improvement on the 64% achieved in Quarter 1

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - September 26 (Q2) Financial Performance Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: Integrated Health & Adult Social Care forecasts a £0.974m underspend at Quarter 2.
findings.detail: The paper describes this as an improvement from the broadly balanced position at Quarter 1. It attributes the position to additional growth funding in the 2026/27 base budget.
findings.matters: Adult social care is a demand-led budget, and a forecast underspend against growth funding is what other councils with similar demographic pressures will compare.
findings.quote: an improvement from the broadly balanced position reported at Quarter 1

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - September 26 (Q2) Financial Performance Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: Children, Families & Education forecasts a £3.400m overspend, £1.4m lower than at Quarter 1.
findings.detail: The paper says the reduction is largely from further forecast use of the Families First grant. SEN transport is forecast at a £1.3m overspend.
findings.matters: Grant funding used to offset children's services overspends is a recurring pressure for councils with statutory SEN transport and placement costs.
findings.figures: £3.400m overspend; £1.4m decrease from Quarter 1; £1.3m SEN transport overspend
findings.quote: This is a decrease of £1.4m from Q1

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - September 26 (Q2) Financial Performance Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: General Fund Balance is now around the level recommended by the S151 officer (10% of net revenue expenditure).
findings.detail: The paper says this follows the approval of EFS. Earmarked revenue reserve levels remain low, and HRA unearmarked reserves remain low.
findings.matters: A general fund balance at the S151 officer's recommended level, alongside low earmarked reserves, is the reserves position other councils and lenders will compare against.
findings.figures: 10% of net revenue expenditure recommended level
findings.quote: Balance is now around the level recommended by the

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - September 26 (Q2) Financial Performance Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: The HRA is forecasting a £2.510m surplus, with £18m of a £27m provision for housing disrepair included.
findings.detail: The paper says the forecast underspend is mainly from reduced interest on borrowing and reduced void loss, offset by repairs overspends on the voids backlog.
findings.matters: The HRA disrepair provision and its use against the surplus is a specific risk for landlords and lenders assessing housing revenue account sustainability.
findings.figures: £2.510m HRA surplus; £18m of £27m disrepair provision included; £2.5m underspend; £18.000m disrepair provision in budget table

daily_post.lead: A first-quarter overspend in the year after a £35.1m outturn overspend shows whether the savings and mitigations are landing, which other councils with similar savings plans would want to see.
